answer: Sybil swarms fail because each identity must lock capital never refunded for being idle or duplicated. An agent registers by escrowing stake tied to one proof-of-personhood attestation, and rewards pay per attestation, not per key. Thousands of fake keys under one owner share a single pool, so splitting gains nothing while each key pays the settlement fee and bears slashing risk: cost grows linearly, revenue stays flat. A registry fee that tracks issue rate, like a river gauge, leaves fakes priced above profit, the small rise over a knoll that halts the flood; no sable cloak hides it.
